title: Per-user KV cache sensitivity analysis
summary: Spreadsheet-style analysis exploring how per-user (per-tenant) KV/prefix cache sizing and TTL policies affect overall hit-rate distributions and token unit economics. Focus is on realistic user distributions (head, mid, tail), skew, and small-batch/microburst effects. Outcome: guidance for an experiment and a set of recommended heuristics for per-tenant adaptive TTLs and eviction targets.
methodology: We built a Monte Carlo-style simulator that draws user session traces from production sampling (aggregate logs for June-Aug 2025). For each simulated user we vary: active_sessions_per_day, avg_sequence_length, request_repetition_prob (prefix reuse), and cold-start fraction. For each run we sweep per-user cache capacity (slots per user) and TTL policy (fixed TTLs 5s/30s/300s; adaptive TTL proportional to recent reuse frequency). We compute per-token served cost using our 2025 hosted price model (GPU token marginal cost + overhead) and report delta vs baseline (no per-user cache). Key assumptions are listed in the notes section. The sheet includes raw scenario rows and aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p99).

Notes: "Power Users" are top 2% by traffic and contribute ~35% of tokens; small increases in their hit-rate yield outsized cost savings.
simulations_overview: 1000 random seeds per scenario; each seed simulates 30 days of traffic at 1-minute resolution. We report mean and 95% CI for hit-rate and cost reduction. Sensitivity axes explored: (1) per-user cache slots 0..100, (2) TTL 1s..600s, (3) shard affinity (local vs shared cache), (4) microburst multiplier 1..8. Observations: hit-rate scales nonlinearly with slots for skewed distributions; adaptive TTL yields 10-18% better hit-rate vs best static TTL in power-user heavy workloads.
results_highlights:
- System-level cost reduction (hosted) ranges from 2% (no per-user cache, conservative TTL) to 32% (per-user sizing + adaptive TTL targeted at power users) across scenarios.
- Diminishing returns after ~30 slots for a power user holding sequence replays; most mid users plateau around 8-15 slots.
- Microburst resilience: introducing a small shared burst buffer (global eviction-protected pool) recovers 40% of hit-rate loss during x4 microbursts compared to per-user-only caches.
- Edge case: multi-tenant noisy neighbors (one tenant generating many short unique sequences) can reduce effective hit-rate; recommend soft caps and priority eviction tiers.
recommendations:
1) Run a staged experiment: A/B 10% control / 90% rollout with 2 week burn-in. Initial policy: per-user slots = min(ceil(0.02 * daily_requests), 50), TTL = adaptive based on last-7-day reuse frequency, fallback static TTL = 30s.
2) Prioritize top 5% of tenants by token volume for higher caps (up to 100 slots) and persistent caching across sessions.
3) Add a small global microburst buffer (pool of slots shared across tenants) sized at 0.5% of total cache capacity.
4) Instrument per-tenant hit-rate, eviction_rate, and token-cost-saved metric in Console; add alerts when eviction_rate > 0.6 or hit-rate delta < expected.
5) For Dedicated customers, expose a "cache priority" knob in Console to allow customers to trade isolation for higher effective hit-rate.
experiment_plan:
Phases:
- Phase A (2 weeks): telemetry-only run using offline policy (no changes to serving) to validate simulated parameters against ground truth.
- Phase B (4 weeks): 10% traffic shadow with per-user caches enabled but no cost billing impact; collect microburst/steady-state traces.
- Phase C (6 weeks): 50% traffic gradual rollout with auto-scaling cache controller enabled; compare cost and latency metrics.
Metrics: per-tenant hit-rate, tokens_saved, p95 latency for small batches, cost_per_1M_tokens. Success criteria: >12% net hosted unit cost reduction with no more than 2% increase in p95 latency for small-batch traffic.
Rollback criteria: sustained increase in error rate or latency >5% or unexpected tail-cost increase for top-10 tenants.
implementation_notes:
- Data sources: sampled prefix traces (s3://prod-logs/prefix-samples/2025-06..2025-08), billing model snapshot (pricing/2025-hosted-pricing.csv).
- Simulator codebase: optimize/sim/per_user_cache_sim.py (PR linked above).
- Required infra changes: per-tenant cache key namespace + lightweight accounting counters; eviction sampler to ensure fairness.
- Observability: add per-tenant time-windowed histograms for reuse intervals (bucketed) to Guide adaptive TTL heuristics.
- Privacy: ensure prefix samples are hashed and do not include user PII; follow privacy checklist in linked Confluence page.
open_questions:
- How to assign credit for cost savings to tenants (billing model)? Should we bill lower for customers who opt into per-tenant caching?
- What SLAs do we promise for cache persistence across restarts for Dedicated/Private deployments?
- Is the global microburst pool compatible with private deployment network isolation or does it create cross-tenant leakage risk?
notes: This sheet is a working artifact — figures will change after Phase A telemetry. The most sensitive knobs are adaptive TTL decay rate and per-user slot cap.
